title: 2D area or perimeter: plug in and combine
subtitle: Area and volume · 33 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **33 of the official questions in Area and volume are this one** — 22 Easy, 8 Medium, 3 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You get a rectangle, square or triangle, either drawn or described with its dimensions, and the question asks for its area or perimeter.
- The question may also ask for the total of two shapes, or what is left when one shape is cut out of another.
- Some choices are expressions in a variable, and one of them is usually the perimeter when the question asks for area, or the other way round.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Check whether the question asks for area (square units) or perimeter (units).
- 2) Write the formula: A = lw, A = s², A = ½bh, or perimeter = the sum of all sides.
- For a right triangle, the base and height are the two legs, so leave out the longest side.
- Add the areas for a combined figure, and subtract for a cut-out.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Type ½·b·h or the sum of the sides to check your number.
It does not help you choose the right formula.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: The wrong choices are perimeter-for-area swaps, the base alone without the ½, and triangle areas that use the hypotenuse as the height.
For an equilateral triangle, you may multiply one side by 4 as if it were a square.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
The wrong choices are perimeter-for-area swaps, the base alone without the ½, and triangle areas that use the hypotenuse as the height.
For an equilateral triangle, you may multiply one side by 4 as if it were a square.
